Mars and Earth water lens equivalents

Depth–time water lenses and integrated suitable-water volumes. Heatmap intensity represents 0–80 °C water per kilometre depth, converted to each planet’s GEL. Definitions and model limits

Wₚ is all assigned unbound interstitial pore water, including allocations in frozen or overly hot cells. Phase-screen liquid uses a pure-water saturation-pressure test, a hydrostatic pore-pressure assumption, and 0–373.946 °C. The 0–80 °C volume is the narrower comparative microbial window; H further applies a tapered thermal score. These quantities must not be conflated. No surface ocean, biomass, salinity, reaction energetics, microbial tolerance census or empirical saturation map is represented.

Mars closure is operational: deepest sampled midpoint with porosity above 10⁻⁵ after thermal and mineral-occlusion tapers. The reference prescribed cap is 22.5 km; 20–25 km joint endmembers are sensitivity cases. Earth has separate continental and oceanic effective domains. All Earth GEL values use Earth’s own area. Sources, assumptions and full-depth data accompany the manuscripts.
